definition: An open-source Nvidia library for building and running optimised inference engines for large language models on Nvidia GPUs.
details: TensorRT-LLM wraps the TensorRT deep-learning compiler with large-language-model specific optimisations and a Python API for defining models, compiling engines and serving them. It implements the techniques that dominate modern LLM serving - paged attention and KV caching, continuous batching, chunked prefill, in-flight batching, speculative decoding and quantization down to low-bit formats - and ships the kernels needed to run them efficiently on datacentre GPUs. Engines are built ahead of time for a target GPU and precision, which is what allows aggressive fusion and kernel selection at the cost of a compile step and some portability across hardware generations. It is one of the main alternatives to vLLM and SGLang, and Nvidia positions it as part of the broader TensorRT product family alongside the core SDK and TensorRT-RTX.
story: Picture an engine rebuilt for one particular road, one particular load and one particular fuel. It will not drive anywhere else, and it was never meant to - but on that road it is faster than anything general-purpose could hope to be. Generality is a tax, and sometimes you are allowed to refuse it. And that is TensorRT-LLM.
